ARCA_West_Poles = 0 | updated = July 24, 2026 }} '''Charles Connor Mosack''' (born January 20, 1999) is an American professional [[stock car racing]] driver. He competes part-time in the [[NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series]], driving the No. 7 [[Chevrolet Silverado#Fourth-generation Silverado / fifth-generation Sierra (GMT T1XX; 2019)|Chevrolet Silverado RST]] for [[Spire Motorsports]] and part-time in the [[ARCA Menards Series]], driving the No. 28 [[Chevrolet SS]] for [[Pinnacle Racing Group]]. He has previously competed in the [[NASCAR Xfinity Series]], [[ARCA Menards Series East]], and [[ARCA Menards Series West]]. ==Racing career== ===Early career=== {{unreferenced section|date=January 2026}} After participating in an on-track [[Mario Andretti]] Racing Experience at [[Charlotte Motor Speedway]], Mosack began his racing career in 2017 in the INEX U.S. Legend Car ranks. Entering his first full season in 2018 at the age of nineteen, he needed just four races to earn his first victory, taking the fourth of five events in the 2018 Winter Nationals at Florida’s Citrus County Speedway. Racing in the Semi-Pro and Open Divisions, Mosack competed at North Carolina’s [[Concord Speedway]], the Summer Shootout Series at [[Charlotte Motor Speedway]], and [[Las Vegas Motor Speedway]], among other events. In 42 starts, Mosack earned twenty victories, 34 top-fives, and 37 top-ten finishes. Among those was a sweep of the National events at Las Vegas, including the Road Course World Finals and Asphalt Nationals. In 2019, Mosack raced Late Models at [[Hickory Motor Speedway]], finishing third in points and taking top rookie honors. He earned seven top-five and 25 top-ten finishes in 27 starts at the venue. ===CARS Solid Rock Carriers Tour/Late Model Racing=== {{unreferenced section|date=January 2026}} In 2019, Mosack made his [[CARS Tour]] debut in the season finale at [[South Boston Speedway]] for [[JR Motorsports]], and he would finish 12th. In 2020, Mosack signed with JR Motorsports to run full-time in the CARS Tour. He was able to pick up three top-fives, eight top-tens, and Rookie of the Year honors as he finished sixth in points in a season shortened to only ten races due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. His performance earned him a spot in the Drivers Edge Development Program presented by Chevrolet, an elite program selecting only six drivers for mentorship and development. In 2021, Mosack would have a reduced Late Model schedule, only running three races in the CARS Tour and also running the Snowball Derby in addition to a few regional events. In 2022, Mosack only ran three races again in the CARS Tour. In 2023, Mosack ran in select Late Model races in addition to his NASCAR and Trans-Am schedule.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} ===ARCA Menards Series=== [[File:Connor mosack (52261686705).jpg|thumb|left|Mosack leading a group of cars at [[Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park]] in 2022]] Mosack was tapped to drive the No. 02 for [[Young's Motorsports]] on May 10, 2021, for three [[ARCA Menards Series]] races that year. Mosack would first make his debut at the [[2021 Henry Ford Health System 200]], ultimately retiring due to a fuel pump problem and finishing sixteenth.{{Cite web|date=May 10, 2021|title=Connor Mosack Joins Young's Motorsports For Limited ARCA Schedule|url=https://www.frontstretch.com/2021/05/10/connor-mosack-joins-youngs-motorsports-for-limited-arca-schedule/|access-date=November 30, 2021|website=www.frontstretch.com|language=en-US}} He would make two more starts that season, finishing with a best of eleventh at the [[2021 Reese's 150]]. In 2022, Mosack was announced to drive in ten races for [[Bret Holmes Racing]].{{cite web|url=https://www.frontstretch.com/2022/01/11/connor-mosack-joins-bret-holmes-racing-for-part-time-arca-slate/|title=Connor Mosack Joins Holmes for Part-Time ARCA Slate|last=Kristl|first=Mark|website=Frontstretch|date=January 11, 2022|access-date=January 19, 2022}} In 2023, Mosack joined [[Joe Gibbs Racing]] for a six-race slate, running at larger tracks where their primary driver, [[William Sawalich]], was unable to race at due to his age.{{Cite web |last=Christie |first=Toby |date=February 2, 2023 |title=Connor Mosack Adds NASCAR Xfinity, ARCA Starts With Joe Gibbs Racing to 2023 Schedule |url=https://tobychristie.com/nascar-regional/arca-menards-series/connor-mosack-adds-nascar-xfinity-arca-starts-with-joe-gibbs-racing-to-2023-schedule/ |access-date=April 29, 2024 |website=TobyChristie.com}} Mosack scored his first career ARCA win at [[2023 Sioux Chief Fast Track 150|Kansas Speedway]], holding off [[Carson Kvapil]] in the final few laps.{{Cite web |last=Branscum |first=Benjamine |date=September 8, 2023 |title=Connor Mosack Conquers Kansas Speedway, Sioux Chief Fast Track 150 For First Career Win |url=https://tobychristie.com/nascar-regional/connor-mosack-conquers-kansas-speedway-sioux-chief-fast-track-150-for-first-career-win/ |access-date=April 29, 2024 |website=TobyChristie.com}} Mosack followed up with his second ARCA win at Kansas, driving for his family-owned team. ===ARCA Menards Series East=== Mosack would make his debut in the [[ARCA Menards Series East]] in the [[2021 General Tire 125]], driving the No. 02 for [[Young's Motorsports]], finishing seventh.{{Cite web|date=May 10, 2021|title=Young's Motorsports Adds Connor Mosack To ARCA Lineup|url=https://www.arcaracing.com/2021/05/10/youngs-motorsports-adds-connor-mosack-to-arca-lineup/|access-date=November 30, 2021|website=ARCA|language=en-US}} He would make one more start in the 2021 season, in a combination race with the [[ARCA Menards Series]], finishing sixteenth. ===Trans Am TA2 Series=== {{unreferenced section|date=January 2026}} Mosack competed in a full season of Trans Am in the TA2 class for [[Scott Lagasse Racing]] in 2021. In fourteen starts, he had ten top-fives, six podiums, and two wins at Watkins Glen. He competed for another full season in 2022.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} ===NASCAR Xfinity Series=== [[File:Connor Mosack 24 Xfinity Sonoma 2023.jpg|thumb|left|Mosack's No. 24 car at [[Sonoma Raceway]] in 2023]] On May 25, 2022, [[Joe Gibbs Racing]] announced that Mosack would make his Xfinity Series debut in their No. 18 car in the road course [[Pacific Office Automation 147|race]] at [[Portland International Raceway|Portland]].{{cite web |url=https://www.jayski.com/2022/05/25/connor-mosack-to-make-nascar-xfinity-series-debut-in-portland-with-joe-gibbs-racing/ |title=Connor Mosack To Make NASCAR Xfinity Series Debut in Portland with Joe Gibbs Racing |website=[[Jayski's Silly Season Site]] |publisher=NASCAR Digital Media, LLC |date=May 25, 2022}} Mosack was announced as the driver for [[Sam Hunt Racing|Sam Hunt Racing's]] No. 26 car at [[Watkins Glen International]].{{Cite web|date=August 3, 2022|title=Connor Mosack Joins Sam Hunt Racing for Watkins Glen International|url=https://www.jayski.com/2022/08/03/connor-mosack-joins-sam-hunt-racing-for-watkins-glen-international/|access-date=August 4, 2022|website=Jayski's NASCAR Silly Season Site|language=en-US}} Mosack returned to [[Sam Hunt Racing]] in 2023, running a majority of the season in the team's No. 24 car.{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Sam Hunt Racing expands for 2023 season; Kaz Grala driving full time |url=https://www.jayski.com/2022/12/08/sam-hunt-racing-expands-kaz-grala-driving-full-time/ |access-date=April 29, 2024 |website=Jayski.com |publisher=[[Jayski's Silly Season Site]]}} He also returned to JGR for three races in the No. 19, with two races ending in DNFs.{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2023 |title=Connor Mosack running 3 Xfinity races with Joe Gibbs Racing in 2023 |url=https://www.jayski.com/2023/02/02/connor-mosack-running-3-xfinity-races-with-joe-gibbs-racing-in-2023/ |access-date=April 29, 2024 |website=Jayski.com |publisher=[[Jayski's Silly Season Site]]}} Mosack ran 24 races and earned a best finish of fifth at [[Watkins Glen International|Watkins Glen]]. He ended the season 28th in points. ===NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series=== [[File:Connor Mosack 45 Truck Las Vegas 2024.jpg|left|thumb|Mosack's No. 45 truck at [[Las Vegas Motor Speedway]] in 2024.]] On June 30, 2022, [[Bret Holmes Racing]] announced that Mosack would make his Truck Series debut in the team's No. 32 truck in [[2022 O'Reilly Auto Parts 150 at Mid-Ohio|the race]] at [[Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course]].{{cite web |url=https://tobychristie.com/2022/06/30/connor-mosack-making-truck-series-debut-at-mid-ohio-for-bret-holmes-racing/ |title=Connor Mosack Making Truck Series Debut at Mid-Ohio for Bret Holmes Racing |website=TobyChristie.com |date=June 30, 2022 |access-date=July 5, 2022}} In 2024, it was announced that Mosack would run a partial schedule with [[Niece Motorsports]] in the No. 45 [[Chevrolet]].{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2024 |title=Niece Motorsports Driver Line-up for the No. 45 Includes Chastain, Sauter, Honeycutt and Mosack – Niece Motorsports |url=https://niecemotorsports.com/niece-motorsports-driver-line-up-for-the-no-45-includes-chastain-sauter-honeycutt-and-mosack/ |publisher=[[Niece Motorsports]] |access-date=February 9, 2024 |language=en-US}} Later that same year, it was announced that Mosack would also run additional races with [[Spire Motorsports]].{{cite web |url=https://www.speedsport.com/nascar/nascar-craftsman-truck-series/mosack-joins-spire-for-select-truck-series-races/ |title=Mosack Joins Spire For Select Truck Series Races |website=Speed Sport |date=April 23, 2024 |access-date=April 23, 2024}} Across nine starts in 2024, Mosack finished with one top-five finish, four top-ten finishes, and a podium finish at [[Homestead-Miami Speedway]]. [[File:Connor Mosack 81 Truck Las Vegas 2025.jpg|thumb|right|Mosack's No. 81 truck at [[Las Vegas Motor Speedway]] in 2025]] On December 3, 2024, [[McAnally–Hilgemann Racing]] announced that Mosack would drive their No. 81 truck full-time in 2025.{{cite web |url=https://bmrnaparacing.com/nascar-craftsman-truck-series/connor-mosack-joins-mhr-for-his-ncts-rookie-season/ |title=Connor Mosack Joins MHR for His NCTS Rookie Season |website=BMR NAPA Racing |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}} On February 21, 2025, Mosack scored his first career NCTS pole for the [[2025 Fr8 208|race at Atlanta]].{{Cite web |last=Srigley |first=Joseph |date=February 21, 2025 |title=Connor Mosack Scores Maiden Truck Series Pole at Atlanta |url=https://tobychristie.com/nascar/truck-series/connor-mosack-scores-maiden-truck-series-pole-at-atlanta/ |access-date=February 21, 2025 |website=TobyChristie.com}} ==Personal life== Mosack graduated from [[High Point University]] with a degree in business entrepreneurship in 2021.{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Greer|url=https://www.hpenews.com/newsletters/hpu-grad-mosack-targets-racing-success/article_1cb8de22-7a30-11ec-8858-936b08b35cce.html|title=HPU grad Mosack targets racing success|newspaper=[[High Point Enterprise]]|date=January 20, 2022|access-date=February 3, 2023}} ==Motorsports career results== ===NASCAR=== ([[Template:NASCAR driver results legend|key]]) ('''Bold''' – Pole position awarded by qualifying time. extract: Charles Connor Mosack (born January 20, 1999) is an American professional stock car racing driver. He competes part-time in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, driving the No. 7 Chevrolet Silverado RST for Spire Motorsports and part-time in the ARCA Menards Series, driving the No. 28 Chevrolet SS for Pinnacle Racing Group. He has previously competed in the NASCAR Xfinity Series, ARCA Menards Series East, and ARCA Menards Series West.
